The sample screenshot shows its actual directory and member activity view; adapt its seeded content to the requested community group. itemRequirements.CRM: Contact records, conversation history, follow-up dates, search and a clear contact detail view.
itemRequirements.ATS: Job listings, candidate applications, pipeline stages, candidate notes and a review workflow.
itemRequirements.Invoicing: Clients, draft invoices, line items, totals, payment status and printable invoices.
itemRequirements.Prism Breaker: A playable brick-breaking game with paddle controls, score, lives, pause, restart and responsive touch controls.
itemRequirements.Mahjong: A playable tile-matching game with valid pair selection, clear rules, shuffle, restart and a win state.
itemRequirements.Racing: Use the Scrap League code in the linked Racing template: twelve authored circuits, four cups, 81 modular car builds, six-car races against five rivals, Time Trial, Daily Spec, keyboard/touch controls, pause/restart, local progress/ghosts and the integrated Track Workshop. Preserve the shared HTML model/compiler, validation, garage presets, Workshop undo/redo, canonical HTML import/export, local drafts and complete offline release checks. Shared online boards and remote Workshop publishing remain disconnected unless separately implemented and verified. Do not replace this with a simpler three-track loop game.
itemRequirements.Business page: A clear value proposition, services, trustworthy proof, contact information and one primary call to action.
itemRequirements.Portfolio: An introduction, selected projects, case studies, accessible project imagery and contact details.
itemRequirements.Link site: A profile with editable links, meaningful labels, accessible touch targets and social destinations.
itemRequirements.Blog: An article index, individual posts, dates, categories and a readable authoring workflow.
itemRequirements.Community group: A community introduction, upcoming events, discussion or resource areas and a clear joining path.
itemRequirements.Photo Album: An accessible image gallery with albums, captions and a detail/lightbox view.
itemRequirements.Booking page: Service options, available slots, timezone labels, booking details and clear confirmation states.
itemRequirements.Journal: Dated entries, an entry editor, chronological browsing, search and an accessible reading view.
itemRequirements.Budget: Income and expense entries, categories, monthly totals, balance and an understandable spending summary.
itemRequirements.Fitness tracker: Dated activity entries, goals, progress, exercise details and a useful weekly overview.

itemPersonalization.CRM: Use my business name as the workspace/account name and my known role, industry, products/services and customer types to tailor the contact fields, relationship labels and follow-up workflow. Prefill only contacts, organizations, dated conversations, commitments and follow-up dates I have actually shared and want included. Distinguish my own business from employers and clients; leave unknown contacts and interactions empty.
itemPersonalization.ATS: Use my business name and known brand, industry, company description, locations and hiring contact in the careers page and hiring workspace. Prefill only actual roles, job descriptions, locations, employment types, salary ranges, application questions and pipeline stages I have shared. Keep unknown roles/details empty; never invent openings, applicants, qualifications or hiring decisions.
itemPersonalization.Invoicing: Use my business/trading name as the invoice issuer and workspace name. Include my known logo, business contact details, billing address, currency, locale, services, rates, payment terms and invoice-number preferences where available and appropriate. Prefill actual clients, line items, project descriptions and due dates only from reliable shared facts. Do not invent tax identifiers, bank/payment details, invoice balances, payments or transactions; ask for missing billing settings.
itemPersonalization.Prism Breaker: Adapt the game theme, paddle/ball appearance, visual preferences, difficulty and keyboard/touch controls to my known tastes, devices and accessibility preferences. Use a known personal or business theme only when relevant. Start scores and achievements fresh; never invent my play history, records or progress.
itemPersonalization.Mahjong: Use known visual themes, tile-style preferences, preferred challenge level, session length, device and accessibility preferences to choose tile contrast, board density, sound and controls. Clarify whether I want solitaire tile matching if uncertain. Start a new game with no invented history or achievements.
itemPersonalization.Racing: Use my known interests in vehicles, settings, visual style, challenge level and preferred device to tailor the car, track theme, control scheme and session length. Offer adjustable controls and motion settings relevant to stated preferences. Do not infer real driving skill or invent race times, unlocked tracks or prior results.
itemPersonalization.Business page: Identify my actual business and use its name in the site title, logo/wordmark text, heading and contact area. Build the value proposition, about section, products/services, audience, locations/service area, public contact details, brand tone and main call to action from facts already known. Use actual approved links/assets; do not substitute a generic company name or invent prices, testimonials, customer logos, credentials or performance claims.
itemPersonalization.Portfolio: Identify whether this portfolio represents me personally or my business/studio; if I own a relevant business, use its actual name and my role consistently. Use known bio, specialties, completed projects, responsibilities, dates, project links, approved imagery and contact/social destinations to populate the introduction and case studies. Do not attribute employer/client work to my business incorrectly or invent clients, awards, outcomes or metrics.
itemPersonalization.Link site: Identify whether this profile is for me or my business; use my actual business name when the intended profile is business-related. Prefill the known display name, bio, approved avatar/logo, website, products/services and verified social/content/contact links. Prioritize destinations relevant to my stated goals and audience. Never guess handles, URLs or offers, and do not mix personal/private destinations with the business profile.
itemPersonalization.Blog: Use my known author identity or actual business name, subject interests, expertise, audience, tone and brand to set the publication name, bio and topic categories. Prefill existing writing, drafts, article ideas and dates only when I have shared them and their status is clear. Do not turn a private memory into a published post or invent past publication dates, citations or experiences.
itemPersonalization.Community group: Use the actual community name and its relationship to my business if known. Populate the introduction, purpose, audience, guidelines, event types, resources, timezone and approved joining/contact links from shared facts. Include real scheduled events only with reliable dates/timezones; do not invent members, quotations, discussions or activity.
itemPersonalization.Photo Album: Organize photos I have actually supplied or made available into albums based on known occasions, projects or subjects, with factual captions and dates only where known. Use my known personal or business identity and visual preferences when relevant. Ask for image files/access if unavailable; do not invent images, people, locations or dates, or pretend you can retrieve an image from a textual memory.
itemPersonalization.Booking page: Use my actual business/practice name, known services, public contact details and relevant brand. Prefill shared service descriptions, durations, prices/currency, working hours, timezone, appointment location/format and cancellation preferences. Confirm availability/calendar integration before offering bookable slots; never invent appointments, availability, payment details or professional credentials.
itemPersonalization.Journal: Prefill dated entries with specific activities, experiences, reflections or milestones I actually discussed, using the dates I supplied. Keep uncertain or undated memories in an undated draft/inbox and ask before assigning a date. Match my known writing tone and journal goals. Distinguish direct recollections from summaries; never invent a day, event, emotion or person to fill a gap.
itemPersonalization.Budget: Use my known currency, locale, budget period, goals and explicitly shared income/expense categories to configure the budget. Prefill actual amounts, recurring bills, frequencies and dates only from reliable information I provided. Separate planned budgets from completed transactions; do not guess balances, income, spending, debt or account details. Keep unknown amounts empty and ask for the minimum needed to calculate useful totals.
itemPersonalization.Fitness tracker: Use my stated activities, goals, units, preferred schedule, equipment and devices to configure tracking fields and views. Prefill workouts only when I shared the activity and reliable date, duration, distance, repetitions or load. Distinguish planned workouts from completed sessions. Do not infer medical conditions, fabricate activity, performance or progress, or turn a stated goal into a completed result.
